plan.goal: Seed primary human hepatocytes in collagen-sandwich culture on a 6-well plate at the standard published plating density across 6 wells.
plan.rationale: Primary human hepatocytes (PHH) are seeded in collagen-sandwich configuration at the standard published plating density of 1.5e5 cells/cm2, which falls within the physiology registry range of 1e5-2e5 cells/cm2 for PHH. PHH do not divide in vitro, so the plating density directly determines the working cell number. A 6-well plate has ~9.6 cm2 growth area per well, giving 1.44e6 cells/well. Standard working medium volume for a 6-well is 2.7 mL/well, giving 16.2 mL total for 6 wells. Collagen-sandwich (thin collagen overlay after attachment) maintains differentiated phenotype.
caveats: PHH are primary human material — BSL-2 containment required.
Confirm the actual 6-well growth area (typically ~9.6 cm2) against your plate lot; some vendors differ slightly.
Collagen-sandwich: allow cells to attach ~2-4 h, then apply a thin collagen overlay (e.g. 0.1-0.2 mg/mL) to restore in vivo-like polarity.
PHH do not divide in vitro — seed at the target density directly; viability should be checked by trypan blue before plating.
Medium volume 2.7 mL/well is the standard working volume; collagen overlay may reduce the effective apical volume.
Verify the specific published protocol's plating density (1e5-2e5 cells/cm2) for the collagen-sandwich method you follow.
